subject.title: Improve read tool handling for binary document formats (.docx, .pdf, .pptx, .xlsx) & Avoid Token Waste on Binary Read

question: Should this issue be solved as a narrow read-tool binary-document fallback, automatic document extraction, or deferred to the broader document/file attachment design?
rationale: The source-level gap is real, but the permanent behavior changes the agent-facing read-tool contract and automatic parsing would introduce dependency and security boundaries that automation should not choose alone.

options.title: Approve Safe Fallback
options.body: Return a clear unsupported-binary-document message for known Office/PDF formats and leave extraction to dedicated tools, plugins, or future document/file support.

options.title: Approve Native Extraction
options.body: Implement bounded extraction through the document-extract/media path after maintainers choose parser dependencies, MIME scope, archive limits, and security rules.

options.title: Defer To File Design
options.body: Keep the read tool unchanged for now and track the behavior under broader provider-native or attachment/document extraction roadmap items.

recommendation.title: Approve Safe Fallback
recommendation.body: Return a clear unsupported-binary-document message for known Office/PDF formats and leave extraction to dedicated tools, plugins, or future document/file support.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest current-main history signal is on the read-tool wrapper and parameter boundary that would own the safe fallback decision.
